title: How does Switzerland use fossil fuels?
description: Switzerland’s trains may run on mostly on renewable electricity, but the country still depends heavily on fossil fuels. Transport accounts for the biggest share, driven by cars, trucks and frequent air travel. At the same time, roughly half of residential buildings are heated with oil or natural gas. Reducing Switzerland's dependence on imported fossil fuels will be critical if it is to meet its net-zero goal for 2050.

title: Ancient Peptide Signals Shape Apple Root Regeneration
description: Root meristem growth factors (RGFs), a class of small peptide hormones that help shape plant roots, may offer a new route to designing better apple rootstocks. By tracing the RGF gene family across 64 plant species and testing its function in apple, researchers found that the family emerged in canonical form in ferns, later contracted and expanded, and diversified markedly within Malus. In apple, the gene MdglRGF1 acted as a brake on adventitious root formation: increasing its expression reduced rooting, while silencing it promoted stronger root growth. The work connects the deep evolutionary history of peptide signaling with a practical target for controlling root architecture in graft-propagated fruit trees.

title: India's ancient knowledge should not remain confined to manuscripts, libraries: Vice President
description: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan emphasised the importance of preserving India's ancient knowledge for future generations. He pointed out that Sanskrit plays a significant role in fields like science, literature, and philosophy. Radhakrishnan expressed concern that great texts must not disappear and highlighted the need for accessibility. The National Education Policy 2020 aims to strengthen the focus on Indian knowledge systems.
